items.stem: A patient's wound culture grows an organism, but the patient has no local or systemic signs of infection. This most likely represents:

options.rationale: Correct: presence of an organism without signs of infection indicates colonisation.
No clinical signs and a wound (not blood) source do not support a confirmed bloodstream infection.
A single colonised patient is not an outbreak.
Culture growth without clinical infection does not by itself indicate sterilisation failure.

items.explanation: Correct: presence of an organism without signs of infection indicates colonisation.

items.stem: Which precaution level is appropriate for a patient with an infection spread by large respiratory droplets?

options.rationale: Correct: droplet precautions (e.g. surgical mask within close range) address large-droplet spread.
A droplet-spread infection requires droplet precautions in addition to standard.
A protective environment is for severely immunocompromised patients, not droplet-spread source control.
Water decontamination does not address droplet transmission.

items.explanation: Correct: droplet precautions (e.g. surgical mask within close range) address large-droplet spread.

items.stem: Select TWO elements required before concluding that an outbreak is occurring.

options.text: A comparison of current case counts against an expected baseline rate
options.rationale: Correct: an outbreak is an increase above the expected baseline, so a baseline comparison is required.

options.text: Use of standardised case definitions to count cases consistently
options.rationale: Correct: consistent case definitions ensure the count is valid.

options.text: A single positive culture from one patient
options.rationale: One positive culture alone does not establish an outbreak.

options.text: Immediate closure of the entire hospital
options.rationale: Closure is a possible response, not a prerequisite for identifying an outbreak.

options.text: A press release to the public
options.rationale: Public communication is not a requirement for determining an outbreak exists.

items.explanation: Correct: an outbreak is an increase above the expected baseline, so a baseline comparison is required.
